text:
alyssa: Heads-up — after merging fe2a9c4 we saw a ~20% p99 increase on small-batch chat tests (B=1-4). Repro on dedicated infra.

matt: Which benchmark and config? sequence length, model, GPU? Any nsys traces already?

alyssa: Benchmark: internal/bench/latency_small_batch (gpt-compat, seq=64, batch=1/2/4), GPU=A10G, cuda 12.1. Attached an nsys capture from before/after runs and a summary. nsys link: https://perf.company/trace/abcd1234 (after), https://perf.company/trace/abcd0000 (before)

perf-bot: nsys upload complete. size=48MB. report: https://perf.company/report/abcd1234

rio: Quick skim of the timeline: after commit there are many more tiny kernels and ~8ms gaps where GPU is idle but host is doing memcpy/kernel launches. Top kernels by time: fused_softmax_forward_kernel, fused_matmul_16x16, and a cuBLAS fallback(batched_gemm_fallback).

sam: That sounds like kernel selection changed. The fe2a9c4 change adjusted heuristics in kernel_selector.cpp to "prefer fused softmax for small seqs". Maybe the fused path now triggers a fallback on some shapes and ends up launching slow scalar kernels.

matt: Can you paste the nsys top kernel table? Also any nvprof or perfetto flamegraphs?

alyssa: Paste from nsys summary:
```
Before (v1.12):
fused_gemm: 1.8ms total, 4 calls, avg=0.45ms
softmax_fast: 0.2ms total, 4 calls, avg=0.05ms
kernel_launch_overhead: ~0.05ms/call
Total GPU busy: ~2.1ms

After (HEAD fe2a9c4):
fused_gemm: 1.8ms total, 4 calls, avg=0.45ms
fused_softmax_forward_kernel: 2.0ms total, 4 calls, avg=0.5ms
extra_small_kernels: 1.6ms total, many calls
kernel_launch_overhead: ~0.25ms/call (increased)
Total GPU busy + stalls: ~5.6ms
```

rio: The profiler annotated CUDA events showing extra memcpy/host-side loops between kernels. Also saw repeated small allocations in device scratch buffer in the new path.

sam: Two hypotheses:
1) fused_softmax path allocates per-call scratch memory which triggers driver syncs on our allocator (we've seen this before)
2) kernel_selector now picks a kernel that isn't optimized for B<=4 and falls back inside kernel to a scalar loop (higher per-call overhead)

alyssa: I tried running with env var REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=softmax_fast to force old kernel — perf returns to baseline. So it's definitely selector/fallback related.

matt: Good repro. Let's bisect to find the exact commit that introduced the problematic heuristic. Use git bisect with a script that runs the bench and compares p99 to baseline. Example:
```
# in repo
git bisect start HEAD v1.12
GIT_TRACE=1 git bisect run ./scripts/ci/bisect_perf.sh --bench latency_small_batch --nsys
```
Script exits 0 if p99 <= baseline, 1 otherwise.
```

perf-bot: Automated bisect completed. First bad commit: 8c3d7a2 — "kernel_selector: prefer_fused for small seq". Bisect traces: https://perf.company/bisect/8c3d7a2

rio: I pulled the trace for 8c3d7a2. Kernel choice log:
```
[kernel_selector] seq_len=64, batch=1 => chosen=fused_softmax_forward_kernel (path=shared_mem)
[kernel_selector] allocate_scratch 48KB => allocator returns via host pinned alloc => slow path
[kernel] fused_softmax_forward_kernel: enters fallback branch for batch<8 => launches scalar_softmax per row
```

sam: So multiple issues: allocator policy + in-kernel fallback. Probably the heuristic didn't consider batch thresholds and shared memory align. The shared_mem path expects batch>=8 to amortize overhead.

alyssa: Patch proposal: revert the 'prefer_fused' flip and add guard `if (batch < 8) prefer_fused=false;` Also change allocator call to use preallocated arena instead of cudaHostAlloc for tiny scratch allocations.

matt: Also add a micro-benchmark in CI: bench/latency_small_batch that runs with B=1,2,4 and asserts p99 delta < 5% against pinned baseline. And add NVTX markers to make nsys smoke cheap.

perf-bot: Quick test of proposed revert branch shows p99 back to baseline on A10G. nsys delta: before: 2.1ms, after revert: 2.2ms (within noise), bad commit: 5.6ms.

rio: I'll open PR to revert the heuristic and add the guard + allocator change. I'll attach perf traces and the nvprof/nvtx smoke tests.

sam: After PR, let's land the perf-check into our release gates so future kernel_selector changes run the micro-bench.

alyssa: Thanks all. Summary added to INF-987 and linked traces. If anyone is free, please review rio's PR; it's high priority.

perf-bot: Incident closed after fix merged to main. Regression reverted in v1.12.1.
